evidence: instruction.md reads cold as a first-person product request from a recruiting team member, written entirely in prose paragraphs with no headings, numbered acceptance list, shall/must table or feature matrix. Line 1 opens 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' and frames the core problem in user terms ('Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.'). Lines 3-9 state needs as lived experience ('I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none', 'If a message arrives while I am reading further up, leave my place alone and just tell me there is something new', 'They must never see our internal notes, why someone was rejected, or anyone else.'). Line 11 delegates exact rules to /instructions/hireops_rules.md and leaves design open ('layout and names are yours', 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout'). Line 13 is the only recipe-like content: Node.js/Express/SQLite, node /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, GET /api/health, /app/app.db/DB_PATH. This is the minimal runtime contract that workbook row 4 requires to be stated, it is phrased conversationally, and it explicitly declines to prescribe layout ('How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.'); it names one route (health), not an endpoint list or file layout, so it does not meet the skill's 'build recipe' defect. Lines 15-17 (copy assets, seed once, accounts/password) are likewise required runtime facts in natural voice. grep for must/shall finds only two natural-language uses (lines 9 and 13). The referenced hireops_rules.md is more structured (numbered sections, bullets, role and wording tables, HTTP codes 401/403/404/409, opening 'Follow them exactly'), but it is a supporting reference note a team would plausibly keep and it explicitly leaves 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages' to the builder; row 1 targets the prompt, and voice consistency between prompt and notes belongs to row 2. Counterexample attempt: a source-text row has no app to pass/fail; the strongest case against Pass would be that line 13 plus the note's status codes make the ask a spec, but the brief remains a recognisable human request and the contract content is mandated by row 4 and the template profile. No runtime evidence is required for this row.
